rv.q: The Last Cabaret On Earth is a surprisingly uplifting and thoroughly entertaining piece about impending doom.

The apocalyptic framing scenes feel somewhat flimsy at first, hinging upon the dubious assumption that a roomful of people facing their last moments alive would choose to hear a cabaret artist tell all about their life and fears, rather than tend to their own affairs.

cn.t: Critics find this apocalyptic one-man show a poignant meditation on mortality, with strong performances elevating the end-of-the-world premise, though reception remains moderately positive rather than rapturous.
